title: Issue summary: When an application passes a stack to PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() to add entries to, and reading fails,…
description: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in OpenSSL versions prior to 3.0.0 in the PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio_ex() function and related functions. When an application passes an existing stack to these functions and the read operation fails, OpenSSL frees all entries in the stack but leaves dangling pointers in the stack structure. This can lead to application crashes or memory corruption if the application continues to use the stack after failure. OpenSSL itself does not pass an existing stack, so this primarily affects third-party applications that do so. The issue is fixed in OpenSSL 3.0.0.
